research_question: What visual features actually identify Sobek across dated museum objects, which features are contextual modules such as solarization or syncretism, and how does that architecture compare with the previously studied multilayer Wedjat eye?

user_supplied_bottle_image.visible_emblem_description: blue circular emblem containing a left-facing crocodilian head/profile with a tall Egyptianizing crown/headdress
user_supplied_bottle_image.rule: The combination of the registered brand name 'Себек' and crocodile-headed Egyptianizing emblem strongly suggests a deliberate Sobek reference, but no manufacturer statement explicitly explaining the logo/name origin was found in the source audit.

brand_sources.claim: Trademark 'Себек', application 2003054587, registered 2005-05-16, owner/applicant Chuhuiv Mineral Water Plant.
Commercial product record for Sebek Lymontyk beverage; brand Sebek; Ukrainian production.
Official site of Chuhuiv Mineral Water Plant / SEBEK brand exists; no explicit Sobek-logo origin statement located in this audit.

high_confidence_identity_features: anthropomorphic male body with crocodile head
crocodile head/profile as the central animal identity carrier
ancient_iconographic_core.important_rule: Crocodile morphology is the strongest identity anchor; crown and solar attributes are contextual modules and cannot alone identify Sobek.

primary_museum_evidence.evidence: Sobek is crocodile-headed and anthropomorphic; wears a tall plumed head ornament with sun disk and twisted ram horns; holds ankh and was-scepter.
Crowned crocodile head identified as Sobek; two plumes, horns and uraei; sun disk indicates connection with the sun god as Sobek-Re; Wadjet cobra is a separate adjacent deity.
Full crocodile Sobek on shrine-shaped plinth; atef crown with sun disk, ostrich feathers, uraei and twisted ram horns; eyes have gold inlays.
Crocodile on shrine represents Sobek; Met notes association with Nile floods/fertility, royal power, later direct association with Re, and broad later syncretism.
Falcon-headed crocodile may combine Sobek with Re; Met also notes possible Soknopaios identity and a possible Horus association through the falcon head.
Sobek is described as the divine violent power embodied in crocodiles and is attested with Horus at Kom Ombo and in the Fayum.
Mummified crocodile from Kom Ombo temple to Sobek and Horus confirms shared cult setting but does not imply deity identity equivalence.
Horus cippus depicts Horus standing on crocodiles as dangerous animals; therefore a crocodile image is not automatically Sobek.

contextual_identity_model.core_rule: Treat Sobek identity and theological context as separate layers. Crocodile morphology carries core identity; crown, solar disk, companion gods, site and period modulate contextual interpretation.

examples.SOBEK: crocodile core may occur without a solar module
examples.SOBEK_RE: crocodile core plus explicit solar association such as sun disk/context
examples.SOKNOPAIOS_OR_OTHER_SYNCRETIC_FORM: crocodile body with falcon head requires source/context resolution rather than automatic Sobek-Re assignment

shared_architecture: Both are composite iconographic systems rather than single invariant silhouettes.
Both require core identity to be separated from contextual modules.
Both can participate in solar associations without being reducible to 'the sun'.
Both interact contextually with Horus while retaining their own identity structure.
Both are vulnerable to false identification if one visually salient feature is treated as sufficient.
critical_differences: Wedjat is a restored-eye symbol with human-eye plus falcon facial morphology; Sobek is principally a crocodile deity represented as crocodile or crocodile-headed anthropomorph.
Wedjat's orientation and eye-side are important variables; Sobek's crown/solar/companion modules appear more informative than left/right orientation for theological context.
Wedjat internal components can be studied as substructures of one eye; Sobek should be decomposed into animal identity, body form, crown stack and attribute/context layers.
No evidence in this audit establishes a Sobek-to-Wedjat morphological derivation, a Wedjat-to-Sobek derivation, or any relation to the six fraction values.
sobek_vs_wedjat.non_bridge_warning: Wadjet the cobra goddess and Wedjat the sound/restored eye are distinct entities; similarity of modern English/Russian spellings must not be used as evidence of identity or lineage.

not_established: exact ancient prototype copied by the designer
specific Sobek-Re rather than generic Sobek intent
exact crown type from the low-resolution label image
manufacturer-authored explanation linking the brand name to the Egyptian god

next_gate.goal: Test whether Sobek can be classified by a reproducible multilayer morphology across periods without using object labels during feature extraction.
tests: Core-identity test: crocodile morphology should classify Sobek better than crown-only features.
Solar-module test: sun disk/crown should distinguish Sobek-Re/solarized contexts from non-solar Sobek without being sufficient for Sobek identity.
Syncretism test: falcon-headed crocodile objects should form a context-sensitive branch rather than being forced into base Sobek morphology.
Control test: Horus-cippus crocodiles and generic crocodiles must prevent species-only overcalling.
Period holdout: freeze feature extraction on training periods and test one held-out period without retuning.
next_gate.promotion_rule: Promote to SOBEK_MULTILAYER_ICONOGRAPHIC_GRAMMAR_CANDIDATE only if core-vs-context separation replicates under period holdout and matched non-Sobek crocodile/crown controls.

highest_admissible_claim: Museum sources support a multilayer model in which Sobek's crocodile morphology is the primary identity carrier, while crown, sun disk, uraei, attributes, companion gods and site/period provide contextual modules including Sobek-Re and other syncretic forms. This architecture is structurally comparable to the contextual multilayer treatment of the Wedjat eye, but no direct Sobek-Wedjat lineage, fraction relation, hidden text, or exact corporate logo provenance is established.
